turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Hale, you can come through. I've got the repeat list printed off the pharmacy system from this morning.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): About time. I've been stuck in that waiting room and my knees are throbbing.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, Mr Hale. Sorry about the wait. This is your routine repeat review, yes?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. And I want something stronger. The paracetamol and the naproxen aren't touching the pain.
[SEG0005] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'm June, his carer. I come four mornings a week. He was up half the night with those knees, so he's a bit sharp this morning.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks for coming, June. Mr Hale, before the painkillers, any allergies to medicines at all?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Both knees, or one worse than the other?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Both. Um, the right one plays up more on the stairs. Been years — four or five, I can't be exact.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any stiffness with that?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Stiff when I first get up, then it eases a bit, and the pain comes back when I walk.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): And what are you taking for it just now?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol, two of the five-hundred milligram tablets, three times — no, four times a day. And naproxen, one of the two-hundred-and-fifty ones, twice a day.
[SEG0014] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He misses the lunchtime paracetamol a lot, mind, if I'm not there to put it out.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you still taking the omeprazole, one twenty-milligram capsule every morning, for your stomach?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I want tramadol. My neighbour swears by it. These ones are useless.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll come to tramadol in a minute. The omeprazole first — twenty milligrams each morning, yes or no?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, every morning. Stomach's fine, that's not the problem.

[SEG0019] person_1 (NURSE): Pharmacy list says paracetamol one gram four times daily, omeprazole twenty milligrams once daily, amlodipine five milligrams once daily, and naproxen five hundred milligrams twice a day. Not two-fifty.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Rubbish. Mine are the little two-fifty tablets. Well, actually, they've always been the two-fifties. Your computer's wrong.

[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): So you're sure it's two hundred and fifty milligrams twice a day, and the pharmacy record says five hundred. I won't change that dose today until we've seen the actual packet.
[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I can read the box tomorrow morning and phone the surgery.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): While I pull the notes up, did you get caught in that rain on the way?
[SEG0024] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Pouring on the ring road. Traffic was crawled right back to the roundabout.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Took us forty minutes for a ten-minute hop. Pointless.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): I heard the Test was rained off again this morning. Typical English summer.
[SEG0027] person_4 (CAREGIVER): My grandson was gutted. He'd got the day off school to watch it and they never bowled a ball.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Cricket. Waste of a day if you ask me. All that standing about.
[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): My dad was the same, glued to it anyway. He reckons they'll get a result at Edgbaston if the weather holds tomorrow.
[SEG0030] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I doubt it. Forecast said more showers. We nearly missed the bus back as well, the 42 was late.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Can we not do the weather. I just want this finished.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Of course. Sorry. Back to the list — the amlodipine, five milligrams once a day for your blood pressure, still taking that?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, every morning with the omeprazole. Can we get on with it.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Just so I'm clear: paracetamol two five-hundred milligram tablets four times a day, though lunchtime doses often get missed; omeprazole twenty milligrams each morning; amlodipine five milligrams each morning for the high blood pressure; and naproxen twice a day, strength not agreed, you say two-fifty, the pharmacy says five hundred.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): That's what I said. And I still want the tramadol.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): I checked his blood pressure before you came in. It was one hundred and thirty-eight over eighty-four, and his pulse was seventy-two.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's acceptable. Let me look at the knees a second. Both are a bit bony and knobbly, there's no redness, and they're not hot.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): They hurt if you poke them. Obviously.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't press. You've got osteoarthritis in both knees, and it's grumbling, especially on the stairs. I don't think adding tramadol is the right thing.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Why not? It's just a painkiller.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): It makes people drowsy and unsteady, and the fall risk isn't worth it when you're already on regular paracetamol and an anti-inflammatory. I'm not going to prescribe it.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): So I just suffer, do I.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Keep the paracetamol regular, including lunchtime if you can, and stay on the omeprazole while you're on naproxen. We'll reissue the repeats as they are, but I won't alter the naproxen strength until June checks the box.
[SEG0044] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll ring tomorrow with whatever's printed on the packet.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please do. And Mr Hale, if the knees get markedly worse before we next meet, book back in sooner rather than sitting on it.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Otherwise I'll see you in six months — sorry, three months — for the next repeat review. Reception can book that on your way out.
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): I'll let them know at the desk.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months of the same useless tablets. Marvellous.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): I know it's frustrating. If the packet shows five hundred, we'll talk about whether that dose is still suitable, but not today.
[SEG0051] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Come on, we'll get the bus if we leave now. The rain might have eased.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't start on the rain again.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Take care, both of you. June, that phone call tomorrow is the useful bit.
[SEG0054] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll do it in the morning.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I go now?
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Mind the step on the way out.
[SEG0057] person_1 (NURSE): I'll walk you back to reception.
